$comment: Body plan overrides for records whose stated limbs do not distinguish the plan, or state it misleadingly. scripts/foundry-module.mjs derives the plan from each record's own traits; anything named here wins instead. Keep the reason with the entry: an override is a claim that the derivation is wrong about a specific creature, and the next person needs to know why. The full derived assignment for all records is in review/reports/foundry-body-plans.md.

reasons.scorpions: Eight Legs with no arms is indistinguishable from a spider in the traits. Seven Monstrous Scorpion records are scorpions; the derivation's general answer, arachnoid, would lose the sting.
reasons.octopuses: Their six extra-flexible arms are written with Foot Manipulators, which the derivation reads as feet-used-as-hands rather than tentacles, so they fall through to arachnoid on their Eight Legs.
reasons.squid: Squid, Giant Squid and Kraken state No Legs (Aquatic) with a ring of arms, but the arm entries do not all carry Extra-Flexible, so the tentacle test misses them and they land on ichthyoid.
reasons.giant praying mantis: States Four Legs and winged flight because its raptorial forelimbs are counted as arms; a mantis stands on six.
reasons.mermen: Fish-tailed humanoids that state No Legs (Aquatic). The derivation sends them to ichthyoid, which has no arms; the Game Aid has a fish-tailed humanoid table that keeps them.
reasons.behir: States Extra Legs (Twelve Legs). The derivation only recognises four, six and eight, so an unusual count falls through to humanoid; a behir is a many-legged serpent.
reasons.axebeak: A flightless bird. With no wings to read it falls through to humanoid, and the derivation has no signal for a two-legged beaked animal.
